SMCI.summary: Super Micro Computer (SMCI) is absolutely on fire in the online investing community right now. Reddit mentions exploded from just 4 in the previous 24 hours to 77 in the last day, pushing it to the 9th most-discussed stock on those forums. Over on Stocktwits, the sentiment is overwhelmingly bullish with 23 bullish tags and zero bearish tags among the messages we sampled. The core reason for all this excitement is a preliminary Q1 earnings release that blew past the company's own guidance. SMCI said it expects revenue between $18.5 billion and $19.5 billion, while its prior guidance was only $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion. That's a massive beat driven by demand for AI platforms. Gross margins are also tracking higher at 12.0% to 12.5% versus the 10.4% to 10.8% they had guided, thanks to favorable customer and product mix. Investors are doing the math and liking what they see: with a market cap around $20 billion and quarterly revenue approaching $19 billion, the stock looks incredibly cheap on a price-to-sales basis. One popular post pointed out that the stock trades at a single-digit P/E and mid-single-digit forward P/E, which many see as absurd for a company growing this fast. There's also relief that the company has a new competent CFO and that past smuggling allegations are in the rearview mirror. The community is calling out short sellers for still trying to push a negative narrative, with one user asking 'How are the shorts still directing the narrative on this stock?' Price targets being thrown around include $40, $60, $100, and even $120 by year-end. Some are calling the current price a great entry point, while others are celebrating those who sold at $32. The mood is euphoric, but investors should remember that this is a preliminary announcement, not the full official print, and the stock has a history of extreme volatility. The bullish case is strong on numbers, but the crowd is clearly in hype mode, so caution is warranted.

GOOGL.summary: Alphabet (GOOGL) is getting a lot of attention online, with Reddit mentions more than doubling from 27 to 56 in the past 24 hours, placing it 10th on the Reddit ranking. On Stocktwits, sentiment is more mixed than SMCI, with 18 bullish tags and 8 bearish tags. The biggest bullish catalyst is a Wall Street Journal report that Anthropic will spend $111 billion on Google Cloud computing, $31 billion on Microsoft Cloud, and up to $86 billion renting Nvidia chips. Investors see this as a huge validation of Google's cloud and AI infrastructure, and they expect more good news from hyperscalers like Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta in the coming weeks. The risk is that crowded bullish positioning makes the stock vulnerable to sharp pullbacks on any negative surprise, while the opportunity is that dip-buyers keep showing up. Overall, the discussion reflects a stock that people love to own but also love to second-guess.
